skill.displayName: Yufluent Clawhub Publish Yufluentcn Comp Scrape

llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate cloud competitor-analysis skill, but it can upload sensitive business data and an API token to a configurable endpoint without enough transport or file-scope safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs network and file input for its purpose, but TOKENAPI_BASE_URL is arbitrary and may use HTTP, while bearer credentials and uploaded datasets are sent through requests.post without URL scheme or host validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is limited to the common requests package and a TOKENAPI_KEY environment variable. The dependency is unpinned, and .env setup is documented, but I found no install-time persistence or credential-file harvesting.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent instructions require cloud execution and allow competitor data or listing inputs to be file paths, but there is no runtime confirmation before uploading the resolved file contents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, services, scheduled tasks, or privilege escalation were found. The code can write an optional output file and includes an unused record_outcome API helper that is underdocumented but not automatically invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: analyze user-provided CSV exports or authorized API snapshots through a Yufluent cloud harness. The name and endpoint use 'comp-scrape' while the docs say it is not an unauthorized scraper, which is ambiguous but not enough to show malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only for data you intend to send to Yufluent, keep TOKENAPI_KEY private, set TOKENAPI_BASE_URL only to a trusted HTTPS service unless you are deliberately using localhost for development, and check every file path passed to the CLI so unrelated secrets or private files are not uploaded.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Cloud submission is expected, but sending the bearer token and payload to an environment-controlled base URL without HTTPS or host validation is not proportionate for sensitive data.
[PE3] expected: The .env references are setup guidance for the user-provided TOKENAPI_KEY, not evidence of credential theft or reading unrelated credential stores.
[TP4] expected: The 'comp-scrape' naming is confusing beside repeated non-scraper statements, but the local artifact only posts user-supplied data to the declared cloud harness and does not contain scraping code.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill lacks enforceable least-privilege limits for destination hosts and readable file paths, which matters because it handles API credentials and proprietary commercial data.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases are broad but still competitor-analysis oriented; this is a usability and accidental-invocation risk rather than standalone malicious evidence.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documentation says cloud execution is used, but the CLI sends payloads without an in-band confirmation or destination/size disclosure.
[SQP-3] expected: The skill is Chinese-first and defaults to zh, while metadata lists several languages; this is a localization limitation, not a security finding.
[SDI-4] expected: The agent-turn fallback may return a message rather than a strict skill result; this is a reliability ambiguity, not evidence of hidden execution.
[SDI-2] unexpected: record_outcome can post arbitrary outcome payloads to a Yufluent endpoint and is not described in the user-facing purpose, though it is not invoked by the main run path.
[SC1] unexpected: requests>=2.31.0 is disclosed but unpinned, so installs are not fully reproducible.
[SC4] unexpected: Because requests is unpinned, the exact resolved version cannot be verified from the artifact alone.
[T09] unexpected: I confirmed the API key is placed in an Authorization bearer header and posted with payload data to URLs derived from TOKENAPI_BASE_URL, which can be HTTP.
[T05] unexpected: I confirmed any existing UTF-8 file path supplied to --competitor-data or --our-listing is read in full and added to the cloud payload without extension, size, workspace, or content validation.
